claim: Replacing the majority-class classifier only in poc_patch.py with a threshold at the midpoint between training class means will increase held-out accuracy on the existing captured train/test data relative to the unchanged baseline.
constraints: Keep the baseline, held-out test split and accuracy measurement unchanged. These fixed evaluation objects do not prohibit changing the treatment classifier cutoff.
Use only the Python standard library, with no network or GPU.

Preserve accuracy as a fraction with higher values better, success when treatment accuracy > baseline accuracy, and falsification when treatment accuracy <= baseline accuracy. These comparisons remain fixed while the treatment classifier cutoff changes.
Run the baseline before the treatment, 3 repeats each, with fixed seed 42.
Report genuine measured values and the limitations of this tiny authored demonstration.

poc_change_scope: Change only the treatment classifier in poc_patch.py to compute the two class means from existing captured training data and use their midpoint as the cutoff, assigning each side to its corresponding class.

independent_variable: Classifier in poc_patch.py: majority-class prediction versus a scalar cutoff equal to the arithmetic midpoint of the two training class means, with sides assigned to their corresponding classes using training data only.
mechanism: The midpoint cutoff assigns each side to the class whose training mean lies on that side. If training class separation transfers to the held-out split, recovered minority-class predictions will outweigh newly incorrect majority-class predictions, increasing accuracy.

metrics.measurement: For each run, use the unchanged accuracy measurement on the unchanged captured held-out test split: correctly classified test examples divided by total test examples. Aggregate separately for baseline and treatment across three repeats.

verification_plan: Before measurements, register this blueprint, accuracy declaration, aggregation and outcome rules; verify that target.accuracy maps to accuracy and its accepted gt baseline comparison converts exactly to factor 1 and offset 0.
Verify all bound input identities, baseline revision and baseline.py entry point, and the identical nonnull environment reference in both resource snapshots.
Review the proposed change to confirm that only poc_patch.py changes and that training class means determine the midpoint cutoff and class-side assignments without consulting held-out labels.

Confirm the baseline, captured train/test data, accuracy measurement and outcome rules remain unchanged; verify the training data supports the specified two-class scalar intervention and report any blocking ambiguity without substituting another intervention.
Verify standard-library-only local CPU execution with no dependencies, network, GPU or external data.
For subsequent authorized measurement, record all three baseline runs before all three treatment runs, using seed 42 for every run and retaining raw execution logs.

Validate accuracy fractions against bounds 0 and 1, compute the mean separately for baseline and treatment, and apply the registered strict-greater success and less-than-or-equal falsification rules without changing thresholds.

Deliver POC files, raw logs and a report with genuine measurements traceable to logs; disclose that this tiny authored demonstration and repeated fixed split do not establish generalization across independent datasets or splits.
